metadata.note: The Housatonic Railroad (chartered 1836 as the 'Ousatonic') ran from Bridgeport up the Housatonic valley to New Milford (1840), the Massachusetts line and West Stockbridge (1842) and Pittsfield (1850), with branches to Danbury (1874), Derby / New Haven (1888-89) and, by lease, the Danbury and Norwalk (1887) with its Ridgefield branch and Wilson Point pier. The New York, New Haven and Hartford leased it on July 1 1892 as its Berkshire Division; Penn Central ran the last Danbury - Pittsfield trains to April 30 1971. Features are split by operator per CLAUDE.md Rule 4 and share geometry across the split; heritage excursions by the modern Housatonic Railroad Company (1984-85) and the Berkshire Scenic Railway Museum (1984-89, 2003-11) are separate tourist_rail features. Drawn spans are the research report's drawable: fields (research/branches/housatonic_railroad.txt), never its wider pax_start/pax_end.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules eff. 30 Sept 1951): NYNH&H Table 12 'New York - Danbury - Pittsfield' and the station index (Botsford and Newtown daggered 'for freight only')
J. W. Karr, The Rail Lines of Southern New England, 2nd ed. 2017, pp. 55-61 - cited only via en.wiki Housatonic Railroad (1836), not consulted directly

properties.geometry_quality: Bridgeport - Brookfield Junction: 26.63 mi drawn against 25.9 mi documented (Fowler line 125). Traced: the Pequonnock River Trail (OSM cycleway/footway on the grade, Bridgeport - Trumbull, 2.8 mi), the Stepney Rail Trail and Newtown Rail Trail plus the abandoned NYNH&H 'Newtown Branch' fragment (Stepney - Botsford, 4.0 mi), the active NYNH&H-tagged Maybrook Line Botsford - Newtown - Hawleyville and west of Hawleyville (10.5 mi), and the Berkshire Line into Brookfield Junction (1.1 mi). APPROXIMATED (straight) legs: Bridgeport station - south end of the Pequonnock River Trail 2.0 mi; Pequonnock River Trail north end (Trumbull) - Long Hill village 2.5 mi; Long Hill - south end of the Stepney Rail Trail 3.4 mi (no OSM or OHM trace of the lifted Trumbull - Long Hill - Stepney grade); a 0.33 mi connector from the Maybrook Line to the Berkshire Line south of Brookfield Junction; and gaps between trail fragments of 0.25, 0.04, 0.23, 0.08 and 0.1 mi - about 8.9 mi approximated in all. ERA CAVEAT: Hawleyville - Brookfield Junction is drawn over the ex-New York and New England (Maybrook Line) track west of Hawleyville and the Berkshire Line, not the Housatonic's own track there, which was abandoned in 1940 (en.wiki Housatonic Railroad (1836)) and is not in OSM; Fowler gives 3.2 mi Hawleyville - Brookfield Jct. Bridgeport starts at today's station; the Housatonic's own Bridgeport terminals were not located.

segments.note: The Housatonic's original main line out of Bridgeport, via Trumbull, Long Hill, Stepney, Botsford, Newtown and Hawleyville. Regular service Bridgeport - New Milford began February 19 1840 (en.wiki Housatonic Railroad; 'February 1840' per en.wiki Housatonic Railroad (1836); first excursion train February 14 1840 per the Newtown Bee); steam from opening, no animal era. Brookfield Junction became a junction only when the Danbury line opened (1868/1874) - the name is used here for the point on the 1840 line. After the 1886/87 lease of the Danbury and Norwalk, Housatonic through trains were routed to Wilson Point / Norwalk instead of Bridgeport (en.wiki Danbury and Norwalk), so this end became secondary well before 1892. Ends 1892 at the New Haven lease (an operator change, not a service end). headway_min is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: the 1840 opening is from en.wiki Housatonic Railroad and Housatonic Railroad (1836) (citing Karr 2017) and the Newtown Bee; the 1892 lease from en.wiki Housatonic Railroad; mileage from Fowler line 125. headway_min and avg_speed_kmh are estimates.

segments.note: The New York, New Haven and Hartford leased the Housatonic on July 1 1892 (en.wiki Housatonic Railroad; July 21 1892 per en.wiki Danbury and Norwalk Railroad) and merged it on March 29 1898 - the merger is not a second split, the New Haven already ran the trains. [OPEN] Passenger service is confirmed to 1920: every station Trumbull - Brookfield Jct carries Fowler's 'b' letter (the New Haven's 1920 public timetable) and none appears in the 1932 timetable. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Source conflict on the end: the 1932 absence points to the 1920s, while a Newtown historian (Newtown Bee) recalls passengers ending 'in the 1940s'; by the September 1951 Official Guide Botsford and Newtown were indexed freight-only. Bridgeport - Stepney was abandoned in 1940 and Brookfield Jct - Hawleyville in 1940 - abandonments, not passenger ends. Freight continued Stepney - Botsford until 1963 and Botsford - Hawleyville survives as freight track. headway_min is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).

segments.note: The New York, New Haven and Hartford leased the Housatonic on July 1 1892 (en.wiki Housatonic Railroad; July 21 1892 per en.wiki Danbury and Norwalk Railroad) and merged it on March 29 1898 - the merger is not a second split, the New Haven already ran the trains. Fowler's letters run x-d (to the New Haven's 1953 timetable) at New Milford, Kent, Cornwall Bridge, West Cornwall, Falls Village, Canaan, Sheffield, Great Barrington, Housatonic, Stockbridge, Lee, Lenox and Pittsfield, and the September 1951 Official Guide Table 12 shows numbered trains (141, 143, 343, 345, 353) with times surviving for New Milford - Cornwall Bridge, alongside labelled bus columns. By 1960 trains terminated at the New Haven's Pittsfield freight yard rather than the Boston and Albany station (Fowler). Smaller stations closed earlier (e.g. Ashley Falls after 1932, Van Deusenville and Glendale after 1920) - station data, not a line change. Ends 1968 when the New Haven merged into Penn Central on December 31 1968. headway_min is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).

West Stockbridge - State Line was the West Stockbridge Railroad, opened August 10 1838; Van Deusenville - West Stockbridge opened with the Berkshire Railroad on December 1 1842; the Housatonic worked it from the February 6 1844 lease (en.wiki Housatonic Railroad). Drawn from 1844: 1838-1844 is omitted because who ran the trains and by what traction is not established (a Rule 5 risk for an 1838 short line), and 1842-1844 because the lease date is the first proven Housatonic year on the West Stockbridge RR. This was the Housatonic's through route to Albany until the 1850 Pittsfield extension made it a branch. Ends 1892 at the New Haven lease. headway_min is an estimate: no timetable for this era was consulted (Rule 3).
